summary.summary_text: 7 potentially deceptive element(s) found among 15 analysed: Misleading urgency (3), Misdirection / confirmshaming (2), Misleading scarcity (1), Social proof pressure (1). Overall risk is high. Review each finding's evidence before drawing conclusions.

findings.evidence: LIMITED TIME OFFER 10% OFF - ENTER CODE \"CASES\" AT CHECKOUT
findings.explanation: The wording creates time pressure (a deadline, countdown or 'ends soon' claim). When the deadline is not genuine or not verifiable, it pushes shoppers to decide before comparing options. Words in this element that most increased the model's score: “time”, “limited time”, “limited”.
findings.confidence_statement: ClearCart is 99% sure this is a fraud/scam (dark pattern) tactic: Misleading urgency.

findings.ethical_recommendation: Only show a deadline if it is real, and state the exact end date/time and time zone. Remove countdowns that reset, and avoid pressure words such as 'Hurry' or 'Last chance'.
findings.short_reason: Deadline or countdown pressure pushes a rushed decision

findings.explanation: The text signals limited stock or high demand. Unverified scarcity claims raise the perceived value of an item and pressure an immediate purchase. Words in this element that most increased the model's score: “left”, “only”, “hurry”.
findings.confidence_statement: ClearCart is 99% sure this is a fraud/scam (dark pattern) tactic: Misleading scarcity.
findings.ethical_recommendation: Show stock levels only when they come from live inventory, as a neutral fact (e.g. 'In stock: 3'). Drop 'Hurry' / 'Almost gone' framing and never display fabricated low-stock messages.
findings.short_reason: Low-stock or high-demand claim pressures an immediate buy

findings.evidence: No, I'll rather pay full price.
findings.explanation: The wording steers the choice through framing rather than information - e.g. a decline option that shames the user ('No thanks, I don't want to save money') or an upsell framed as the default path. Words in this element that most increased the model's score: “i”, “no”, “price”.
findings.confidence_statement: ClearCart is 99% sure this is a fraud/scam (dark pattern) tactic: Misdirection / confirmshaming.

optimisation.method: exact per-element minimisation over a finite candidate set (one batched model call)
optimisation.objective: minimise the redesigned CDI (model-estimated content pressure + by-construction choice/obstruction terms)
constraints: no added facts or offer words
non-empty and changed (except the original baseline)
optimisation.optimality: content pressure is monotone non-decreasing in each element's score and constraints are per-element, so the per-element minimum is the global minimum over the candidate space
optimisation.tie_break: within 0.005 of the best score, prefer an actual change over the unchanged original, then the smaller word-level edit distance
optimisation.caveat: The objective is the classifier's own indicator and can exploit its label biases; all candidates are shown.

counterfactual.label: Model-estimated reduction: the redesigned text is re-scored by the same classifier. This is not a measured change in consumer behaviour.
